newsitem.title: USA: Accused pleads not guilty in Levin murder case.
newsitem.headline: Accused pleads not guilty in Levin murder case.

text.p: A man accused of killing the son of Time Warner chairman Gerald Levin says he was an unwilling participant who thought he was going to rob the victim, according to court papers released Thursday.
Montoun Hart, 25, and Corey Arthur, 19, are accused of stabbing and shooting Jonathan Levin in his Manhattan apartment. The badly decomposed body of the high school teacher was found June 2.
Hart pleaded not guilty to murder and robbery charges at his arraignment Thursday.
In court papers, Hart said in conflicting statements that he was an unwilling participant and that he thought he was going to Levin's apartment with Arthur to buy marijuana.
Then he said he agreed to help Arthur rob Levin, whom Arthur had as an English teacher at New York City's Taft High School, the court papers said.
Once inside the apartment, Arthur "pulled a black revolver on the white dude," the papers said.
Hart said Arthur used duct tape to bind Levin's hands, feet and mouth. He also said he saw Arthur with the gun "and then I heard a shot," according to the court documents.
Police believe Levin was tortured by the two men with a steak knife until he revealed his personal bank code number and that his attackers withdrew $800 from his account.
If convicted, Hart faces life in prison. Arthur, a convicted drug dealer who was out on parole, is to be arraigned July 7.
The city medical examiner said Levin was slashed in the chest and throat with a knife and shot in the head. Police believe the attack took place two days before his body was found.
